title: Conversion Overdue
logline: A trafficked scam operator on the Myanmar border inherits a fabricated romantic persona and engages in a complex, intimate con with an American man who knows he's being conned but remains captivated, blurring the lines between deceit and genuine connection.

scenes.beat: The operator, Kyan, begins his shift and is assigned a romantic account already six months deep; he reads the entire archive of messages to understand the fabricated relationship with the American, Mark.
Kyan studies the persona guidelines and notices subtle language quirks, identifying the previous operator's unique typing style and emotional inflections.
In his first unscripted message as 'her,' Kyan includes an honest, personal detail that breaks protocol; Mark immediately notices and responds with delight, deepening his emotional investment.
Mark continues to withhold deposits, prompting supervisors to flag Kyan's conversion ratio, increasing pressure on him at the compound.
Mark questions the authenticity of the photographs, tactfully revealing his suspicion without confrontation; Kyan and Mark mutually sustain the illusion despite this tension.
The previous operator, Aung, unexpectedly returns to the account, creating a complicated dynamic between him, Kyan, and Mark.
Kyan becomes jealous of Aung’s earlier messages that built the relationship foundation, feeling inadequate and conflicted about his role.

During a 3 AM conversation, Mark shares an intense philosophical reflection on Kierkegaard’s concept of despair, while the scam dashboard flashes multiple CONVERSION OVERDUE alerts, amplifying operational stress.
Supervisors introduce A/B testing on emotional vulnerability in messages, forcing Kyan to balance genuine connection with manipulative tactics under threat of punishment.
Kyan accidentally reveals a personal truth in a message, breaking persona guidelines; supervisors reprimand him, but Mark perceives it as intimacy, complicating their interactions.
The compound experiences a violent raid and partial collapse, disrupting operations and scattering workers, including Kyan and Aung.
Amid the chaos, Kyan and Aung confront their intertwined roles in the scam, deepening their internal conflicts about identity and deception.
Kyan escapes the compound and arranges a real-world meeting with Mark, driven by a desperate need to reconcile the fractured personas.
Mark arrives, and they meet face-to-face; Mark realizes the messages he treasured most were written by Aung, not Kyan, confronting both men with the layered realities of their relationship.
They part without resolution, each grappling with what was real and what was constructed, leaving their connection suspended between truth and fiction.
